workflows.name: Storage Program Strategy, Product Portfolio & Business-Model Design

Automation Opportunity: - Site-suitability scoring (parking area, trade-density, competitor-storage gap) from GIS/customer-data; capex/payback template tied to real-estate & FP&A actuals
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: business case board/leadership-approved (VS-36); entity & tax-structure Tax-reviewed (VS-79); capex within VS-35/VS-40 approval matrix
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-97 (real estate), VS-35/VS-40 (capex), VS-79 (tax), VS-100 (legal), VS-36 (governance); W5034 (site selection), W5039 (yield)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Demand-misread risk**: Building storage where renovation/project demand won't fill units → stranded capex; mitigated by site-level demand modeling & phased pilot
- **Entity/tax-structure risk**: Wrong legal entity or VAT/percentage-tax treatment on rentals → restate & penalty exposure (VS-79); mitigated by Tax sign-off at step 3
- **Cannibalization risk**: Diverting backroom space needed for omnichannel fulfillment (VS-04/VS-93); mitigated by space-allocation governance with DC/Store Ops
System Touchpoints: - FP&A/strategy (VS-17.4/VS-33); real-estate/portfolio (VS-97); fixed-asset/capex (VS-35/VS-40); legal entity master (VS-29); tax (VS-79); storage property-management module (new capability — W5038/W5039)
Time Estimate: - ~6–10 weeks annual strategy + per-site business case (~2 weeks/site)

steps.activity: Set the storage business strategy & operating model: the product portfolio (on-site self-storage units, drive-up units, climate-controlled, vehicle/boat/RV parking, portable containers, mobile on-demand storage), the make-vs-partner-vs-franchise model, the rollout sequence (which of the 200 stores have the parking/yard footprint and the demand), and the KPIs (occupancy, rate/unit, NOI margin, cross-sell attach)

Build the business case & capital model: capex per unit, breakeven occupancy, payback, cannibalisation check vs BuildRight's own backroom space (VS-04), and the recurring-revenue/NOI contribution to the group P&L (links VS-17.4)

Govern & approve: board/leadership sign-off (links VS-36), legal-entity placement (which of the 5 entities owns the storage — typically Property Mgmt Inc.), and the regulatory/tax posture (VAT on rentals, percentage-tax vs VAT, LGU business-permit scope) with Legal/Tax (VS-79)

fields.Frequency: Per candidate site; ~5–10 new storage sites/year at maturity

workflows.name: Storage Site Selection, Real-Estate Acquisition & Unit-Capacity Planning

Automation Opportunity: - GIS-based demand/supply scoring; automated zoning/LGU-permit status feed; capacity-mix optimizer
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: site acquisition within VS-97 real-estate approval; lease terms Legal-reviewed (VS-42); LGU/BFP feasibility confirmed before capex commit
Cross-references: - links to VS-97 (real estate), VS-42 (lease admin), VS-20 (build), VS-166 (permits), VS-07 (store footprint), W5033 (strategy), W5037 (build-out)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Zoning/permitting risk**: Storage use not permitted at the site → blocked build or LGU violation; mitigated by zoning/LGU feasibility check at step 2 (links VS-166)
- **Capacity-mismatch risk**: Wrong unit-size mix for local demand → chronic vacancy in large units, waitlist in small; mitigated by demand-driven mix modeling
- **Footprint-conflict risk**: Storage consuming customer parking needed for basket/large-item pickup (VS-171/VS-162); mitigated by Store Ops sign-off
System Touchpoints: - Real-estate/portfolio & GIS (VS-97); site/property master (VS-29); lease administration (VS-42); zoning/LGU permit tracking (VS-166); capacity-planning analytics (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~4–8 weeks/site for screening + acquisition + capacity plan

steps.activity: Screen candidate sites against the storage criteria: available parking/yard/side-lot area (vs selling-area need VS-07), access (drive-up vs interior), zoning/LGU allowance for storage use, population & competitor-storage density, and B2B-trade density (contractors needing jobsite staging)

Acquire/secure the footprint: own-build on BuildRight land (VS-20), lease adjacent/under-used land (VS-42), or partner with a third-party facility (W5040); negotiate terms, secure LGU clearance, and confirm BFP/zoning feasibility for a storage occupancy
Plan unit capacity & layout: the unit count and size mix (5'×5' to 10'×30'+ climate/drive-up/RV), aisle/corridor, office, and the build-out scope handed to facility design (W5037)

fields.Participants: Pricing (VS-01.2), FP&A (VS-17.4), Marketing (VS-14), Store/Property Manager, Legal (rate-disclosure)
fields.Trigger: Site capacity plan (W5034); pricing review; competitor rate change

workflows.name: Storage Unit-Type Mix, Rate Card & Pricing Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - Competitor-rate scraping → rate-card recommendation; dynamic rate optimizer (W5039)
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: rate card FP&A/CFO-approved; advertised rates RA 7394-disclosed (VS-118); discounts margin-controlled
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2 (pricing), VS-57 (competitor), VS-118 (price integrity), VS-13 (loyalty), VS-14 (promotions); W5039 (yield), W5038 (lease terms)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-pricing risk**: Street rates below market → NOI leakage; mitigated by competitor monitoring + yield engine
- **Price-integrity risk**: Advertised rate excluding mandatory fees → RA 7394 Consumer Act exposure; mitigated by all-in rate disclosure (Legal, VS-118)
- **Discount-leakage risk**: First-month-free/auto-pay discounts not tracked to margin; mitigated by FP&A tie-out
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/rate-card engine (VS-01.2); FP&A margin (VS-17.4); competitor intelligence (VS-57); loyalty/member (VS-13); RA 7394 price-integrity (VS-118); storage PMS rate module (W5039)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks initial rate card; ~1 week quarterly review

steps.activity: Define the unit-type catalog & dimensions: small (closet/locker), medium (1BR-apt), large (2BR-house), climate-controlled, vehicle/boat/RV parking, and the portable-container equivalents

Set the rate card & pricing architecture: street rate vs in-place rate, discounts (first-month-free, long-term), auto-pay discount, insurance/coverage options, and the price-integrity/disclosure (RA 7394) compliance of advertised rates

Position vs competitors & link to yield: feed competitor-rate monitoring and the dynamic yield/occupancy engine (W5039), and align promotions with Marketing (VS-14) and trade-pro/member discount (VS-13)

fields.Trigger: Strategy approval (W5033); capacity plan; fleet refresh

workflows.name: Portable & Mobile Storage Container-Fleet Strategy, Sizing & Procurement

Automation Opportunity: - Container GPS/telematics → asset tracking (W5053); fleet-sizing model from demand forecast (W5055)
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: container capex within VS-35/VS-40 matrix; insurance coverage VS-26-confirmed; asset tagging/reconciliation (links VS-111)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet), VS-35/VS-40 (assets/capex), VS-111 (returnable-asset pattern), VS-26 (insurance), VS-56 (3PL); W5045 (container delivery), W5053 (container maintenance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fleet-undersizing risk**: Containers out → lost rental & customer churn; mitigated by fleet-to-demand ratio & rebalancing (W5053)
- **Asset-loss risk**: Container theft/abandonment at customer site → PHP ~30–80K loss each; mitigated by GPS/telematics, deposit (W5042)
- **Delivery-cost risk**: Costly tilt-truck delivery eroding margin; mitigated by route density (VS-06) & 3PL option (VS-56)
System Touchpoints: - Fleet/asset management (VS-06/VS-35); procurement (VS-03/VS-34); insurance (VS-26); container-asset tracking (links VS-111 RTI pattern); title/registration (VS-29)
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks fleet strategy; ~6–8 weeks per procurement batch

steps.activity: Size the container fleet & set the mix: 8'/16'/20' portable steel containers + tilt-bed/deliverable "mobile" units, the home/jobsite-delivery model (PODS-style), fleet-to-customer ratio, and the depot/return network per DC (VS-04)

Procure & take delivery: container vendor selection, spec (wind/water-tight, lock-box, ISO/certified), title/asset tagging, and fixed-asset capitalisation (VS-35); plan the delivery flatbed/tilt truck fleet or 3PL (VS-06/VS-56)
Govern fleet risk & insurance: container all-risk/CTPL-equivalent for the delivery vehicle, theft/vandalism coverage, and the customer liability waiver (W5042) with Insurance/Legal (VS-26/VS-100)

workflows.name: Storage Facility Design, Build-Out, Security & Access Infrastructure

Automation Opportunity: - IoT door-alarm/CCTV analytics; access-control→PMS auto-provisioning of tenant credentials
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: BFP FSIC & LGU occupancy before opening (VS-166); HSE sign-off (VS-24); access-control audit trail (W5050)
Cross-references: - links to VS-20/VS-109/VS-112 (build), VS-138 (IFM), VS-23/VS-159 (security), VS-24 (HSE), VS-166 (permits); W5043 (access), W5050 (security ops), W5052 (fire/life-safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire-safety risk**: Non-BFP-compliant partitions/suppression → fire spread, FSIC denial, store closure; mitigated by fire-engineer design + FSIC before opening (VS-24/VS-166)
- **Security-gap risk**: Insufficient CCTV/access → theft and customer-liability claims; mitigated by individual unit-door alarms + access audit (W5050)
- **Commissioning-delay risk**: Missing FSIC/LGU permit blocks go-live; mitigated by permit calendar (VS-166)
System Touchpoints: - Construction/PMO (VS-20/VS-112); facility/maintenance (VS-138); security/CCTV/access (VS-23/VS-159); IT (VS-27); BFP/LGU permit register (VS-166); HSE (VS-24); access-control/gate system (links VS-164 smart-locker pattern)

steps.activity: Design the facility: unit partitions, climate-controlled zone, drive-up doors, aisle/loading, office, lighting, fencing, and the BFP Fire Code / OSH compliance (fire-rated partitions, detection/suppression, ventilation, egress)

Install the security & access infrastructure: perimeter fencing/lighting/CCTV (VS-23), electronic unit-door locks & gate access-control (individual unit alarms), and the access-credential system that gates tenant entry (W5043) — integrated to IT (VS-27) and corporate security (VS-159)
Commission & certify: BFP Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC), LGU occupancy/permit-to-operate (VS-166), HSE sign-off (VS-24), and IT/security-system acceptance before first move-in

workflows.name: Storage Lease/Rental Agreement, Terms & Insurance Program Administration

Automation Opportunity: - E-signature lease execution; lease→billing auto-sync; rate-change notice automation
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: master lease Legal-approved (VS-100); tenant data RA 10173-consented (VS-91); lien clause Civil-Code-compliant (W5047)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100 (legal), VS-42 (lease admin), VS-16 (O2C), VS-26 (insurance), VS-91 (privacy), VS-22 (compliance); W5042 (move-in), W5044 (billing), W5047 (lien)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability-misframing risk**: Mis-drafted bailment language exposing BuildRight to stored-goods loss claims; mitigated by Legal master lease + no-bailment disclaimer
- **Lien-legality risk**: Lien/disposition clause not RA-drafted → unlawful unit clearance (W5047); mitigated by Legal + Civil-Code-compliant lien process
- **Privacy risk**: Tenant personal/financial data (RA 10173); mitigated by consent + VS-91 controls
System Touchpoints: - Contract/lease master (VS-29/VS-42); O2C/billing (VS-16); e-signature; insurance (VS-26); privacy/consent (VS-91); storage PMS lease module
Time Estimate: - ~4–8 weeks initial master lease; ongoing lease administration

steps.activity: Draft the master lease/rental agreement: term (month-to-month vs fixed), rate/fee schedule, security deposit, late-fee/delinquency lien terms (links W5047), prohibited-goods clause (W5051), access rules, and the landlord-liability/no-bailment disclaimer (Civil Code)

Set up the tenant insurance / damage-waiver program: mandatory tenant insurance or BuildRight-sold damage waiver, claim handling, and the data-privacy/consent on tenant data (RA 10173) with Insurance/Compliance (VS-26/VS-91)
Operationalise lease administration: e-signature execution, lease master in the storage PMS, auto-renewal, rate-change notice, and O2C/billing integration (VS-16)

workflows.name: Storage Occupancy/Yield Management & Dynamic Rate Optimization

Automation Opportunity: - RevPAU-optimizing dynamic rate engine; churn-risk scoring → automated retention trigger
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: rate changes within W5035 framework; discounts margin-controlled; churn/delinquency reconciled to O2C (VS-16)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2 (pricing), VS-57 (competitor), VS-28 (analytics), VS-13 (CRM), VS-14 (retention); W5035 (rate card), W5044 (delinquency), W5054 (occupancy analytics), W5055 (forecasting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Yield-leakage risk**: Holding street rates flat as occupancy rises → foregone revenue; mitigated by dynamic rate engine
- **Discount-addiction risk**: Over-reliance on first-month-free → brand/price erosion; mitigated by discount-discipline in W5035
- **Churn-blindness risk**: Undetected move-out drivers → occupancy erosion; mitigated by churn analytics + retention outreach
System Touchpoints: - Storage PMS yield/revenue module; analytics/BI (VS-28); pricing engine (VS-01.2); competitor intel (VS-57); CRM/loyalty (VS-13); O2C/delinquency (VS-16/W5044)
Time Estimate: - ~continuous; ~1–2 days/month per site for rate review

steps.activity: Monitor occupancy & demand by site/unit-type: physical vs economic occupancy, vacancy by size, lead-to-lease conversion, and seasonality (links W5055)

Optimize rates dynamically: street-rate vs in-place-rate spread, move-in discounts vs occupancy, and site-level rate adjustments that maximise revenue per available unit (RevPAU) — governed within the rate-card framework (W5035)
Act on churn & delinquency: identify at-risk/move-out tenants, trigger retention outreach (Marketing VS-14), and feed the delinquency workflow (W5044)

workflows.name: Storage Operator Partner, Franchise & Third-Party-Manager Network Management

Automation Opportunity: - Operator performance dashboard; automated revenue-share reconciliation against operator PMS feed
Controls: - CTL-752 (ensure controlled execution — Storage Portfolio Strategy, Site Selection & Unit/Container Capacity Planning (PA-174.1).)
- CTL-752: operator vetting per VS-161/VS-167; audit rights in contract; royalty reconciled (VS-16)
Cross-references: - links to VS-161 (TPRM), VS-167 (vetting), VS-100 (legal), VS-16 (O2C/royalty), VS-21/VS-22 (audit/compliance), VS-146 (CX); W5033 (strategy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Brand-damage risk**: Under-performing/non-compliant operator tarnishing BuildRight brand; mitigated by operating-standard contract + audit (VS-21)
- **Revenue-leakage risk**: Mis-reported operator revenue → royalty short-pay; mitigated by audit rights + reconciliation (VS-16)
- **Concentration risk**: Over-reliance on one operator; mitigated by portfolio diversification
System Touchpoints: - Contract master (VS-29); O2C/royalty billing (VS-16); TPRM (VS-161); compliance/audit (VS-21/VS-22); CX assurance (VS-146); brand standards (VS-14)

steps.activity: Select & onboard operators/franchisees/third-party managers: define the operating-standard & brand-experience bar, screen (financial, operational, integrity — VS-161/W167), and contract the franchise/management agreement with Legal
Govern performance & compliance: monitor operator occupancy/revenue/NOI vs standard, customer-experience (VS-146), and regulatory/safety compliance (BFP/OSH/RA 10173), with audit rights
Manage revenue share / royalty & exit: revenue-share/royalty billing/reconciliation (VS-16), dispute resolution, and the offboarding/transition path
